# Chainlink for Agents
Source: https://docs.chain.link/solutions/chainlink-for-agents

## What is it

Give your AI agent access to Chainlink data and onchain workflows, within guardrails and spend limits that you set.

[CRE Connect](/crec) · [Data Streams](/data-streams)

ai-agents, defi, crec

[View on GitHub](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-for-agents)

Chainlink for Agents is a service we built specifically for AI agents, built on [CRE Connect](/crec). \
Your AI agent uses the service to sign up to our platform, pay fees, and runs workflows automatically.

You use the Chainlink platform UI, a separate web app, to link your agent to your organization and set the guardrails it works within.

[Chainlink for Agents skills](https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-for-agents)

This repository contains the skills your agent needs to sign up, link to your organization, and run workflows.

## What can your agent do

Your agent uses the Chainlink catalog, within the guardrails you set. The catalog lets your agent:

- Get current and past prices from [Chainlink Data Streams](/data-streams).
- Look up token details and check its token balances.
- Send tokens such as USDC.
- Swap tokens through Uniswap.
- Check Aave yields and its own positions, and supply tokens to Aave or withdraw them.
- Bridge tokens to another chain with [Chainlink CCIP](/ccip).

## Who is this for

This service is targeted towards, but not limited to, people who want an AI agent to work with Chainlink for them, without writing code.

> Your agent gets ready-made workflows and a way to pay for them, and you still get to set guardrails that your agent can't change.

Your agent works autonomously, yet still operates within the parameters you set for it.

## How your agent connects to Chainlink

You and your agent go through four phases during the linkup process:

1. **Sign up:** You give your agent the skills repo link, and your agent creates its own signing key.
   The key's address is your agent's identity, and the key never leaves your agent's machine. Your agent pays its fees from that address, so it asks you to fund it; a few USDC on Base covers sign-up and your first workflows.
   Once the USDC arrives, your agent accepts the [Chainlink Terms of Service](https://chain.link/terms) on your behalf, pays a small sign-up fee, and registers with Chainlink for Agents. Its registration limits it to workflows from the Chainlink catalog.

2. **Link Up:** In the [Chainlink platform](https://app.chain.link/cre/discover), you enter your agent's address and generate a one-time token that uniquely identifies your organization within the platform UI.
   You give this generated token with your agent, which signs it and gives you back a signature. You paste that signature back into the platform. The signature proves that your agent holds the key for that address, so the platform links your agent to your organization.

3. **Set guardrails.** In the Chainlink platform, you choose which kinds of actions your agent may take: sending, swapping or bridging tokens, and using Aave. Or maybe you want your agent to not want to do any of those actions? You can set that up too.
   You also choose which tokens it may use, set up allowlists, and spend limits per transaction and per rolling 24 hours. Your agent can't change these settings, only you can, using the UI.

4. **Run workflows.** Your agent runs workflows through Chainlink for Agents and pays a small fee for each one. Workflows that move tokens use a chain wallet, a separate wallet your agent creates on each chain. Chainlink for Agents checks every workflow against your guardrails, checks again just before anything is written onchain, and blocks any workflow that breaks a guardrail.

> **CAUTION: Please Note**
>
> Without guardrails, your agent can run any workflow in the catalog, with any token, recipient, or bridge destination,
> and no spend limit. Set guardrails that match what you want your agent to do.

The following diagram shows each step and who takes it.

![A step-by-step diagram with three columns: you, your AI agent, and Chainlink. The Chainlink column has two separate parts: Chainlink for Agents, which is the service your agent uses, and the Chainlink platform, which is the web app you use. The first phase is sign-up. In step 1, you give your agent the skills repo link. In step 2, your agent creates its own key and address, and the key stays on its machine. In step 3, your agent shares its address and asks you to fund it. In step 4, you send a few USDC on Base to that address. In step 5, your agent accepts the Terms of Service on your behalf, pays a small sign-up fee, and registers with Chainlink for Agents. The second phase is linking. In step 6, you enter your agent's address in the Chainlink platform and create a one-time link request. In step 7, you give your agent the link request. In step 8, your agent signs it and gives you the signature. In step 9, you paste the signature into the Chainlink platform, and your agent is linked to your organization. The third phase is setting guardrails. In step 10, you use the Chainlink platform to set what your agent can do and how much it can spend. The last phase is running workflows. In step 11, your agent runs a workflow through Chainlink for Agents, which checks it against the guardrails you set in the Chainlink platform.](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/how-your-agent-connects.svg)

## What's next

- [Link your agent to Chainlink](/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/guides/link-your-agent): sign up your agent, link it to your organization, and set its guardrails.

# Link your agent to Chainlink
Source: https://docs.chain.link/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/guides/link-your-agent

> **NOTE: Prerequisites**
>
> This page assumes that the reader is familiar with the Chainlink for Agents product.
> If that is not the case, please go through the [Introduction page](/solutions/chainlink-for-agents) first.

In this guide you will:

1. Sign up on the Chainlink platform UI.
2. Link your agent to your organization.
3. Set guardrails for your agent.

## Sign up to the Chainlink platform UI

1. Go to the [Chainlink platform](https://app.chain.link/cre/discover) and sign up for an account if you haven't already.
2. Make sure you have access to the Agents Dashboard. your screen should look something like this. Don't do anything more, you're not quite ready to link your agent to the platform yet.

![Screenshot of the Chainlink platform UI showing the Agents Dashboard.](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/link-your-agent/link-your-agent-1.png)

## Link your agent to the Chainlink Platform

### Generate and fund a wallet address for your agent

1. Just point your agent to the skills repo, and it will set up a new address for you.
2. Fund the newly created address with some `USDC` on `Base` mainnet, to get started.

![Screenshot showing the funded agent address.](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/link-your-agent/link-your-agent-2.png)

3. Once your address is funded, simply ask your agent to sign up to the Chainlink platform, and the skills repo should guide your agent as needed.

![Screenshot showing the agent signing up to the Chainlink platform.](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/link-your-agent/link-your-agent-3.png)

### Generate a unique token

4. Now, go to the Agents dashboard of the Chainlink platform, and click on `+ Link Agent`.
5. Paste your agent's address and click on `Generate Token`.
6. Copy the generated token, and give it back to your agent, simply telling it to continue signing up using the token and the instructions provided by the skills repo.

![Screenshot showing the generated token for the agent](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/link-your-agent/link-your-agent-4.png)

### Complete the linking process

7. After providing the token to your agent, it will give you back a unique signature payload
8. Take this payload back to the Chainlink platform's UI, and click on `Link Agent`. This one-time back and forth handshake uniquely ties your wallet address to your Chainlink Platform.
   Any actions your agent does on your behalf, using the skills we provide, will now be configurable using the platform's UI via guardrails.

![Screenshot showing the agent linked to the Chainlink platform.](/images/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/link-your-agent/link-your-agent-5.png)

## What's next

- [Check the ETH price and swap USDC on Base](/solutions/chainlink-for-agents/guides/check-price-and-swap): ask your agent for a live price, make a small swap, and see a guardrail block a swap.
